q: Does the paper's contextuality verdict survive when Hamiltonians are reduced to the exact reduced form used in each cited experiment (Hempel/Peruzzo/Nam), rather than default OpenFermion JW/BK transforms with heuristic active-space choices? Concretely, do we recover the paper's |S| values (5, 8, 13, 22) as well as the yes/no verdict?
basis: In our replication, |S| differs from Table I by 3x-9x for the larger molecules. The verdict is invariant under the reductions that trim S, but we never reconstructed the actual experimental Hamiltonians, so a subtle representation-dependent flip is not ruled out at the boundary cases (e.g., HeH+ with CD0=0.38 is close to the non-contextual boundary).
next_steps: For each cited experiment: (i) pull the exact Pauli list from the experiment's SI or code repo, (ii) run the paper's Theorem 3 classifier on it, (iii) confirm |S| matches Table I to within symmetry-equivalent rewrites, (iv) confirm the contextuality verdict matches, (v) if any verdict flips, document which reduction step introduces the change. Estimated cost: 1-2 hours on CPU per molecule, no paid APIs.

q: For a non-contextual VQE instance (e.g., 2-qubit H2), can one actually construct and evaluate the explicit noncontextual hidden-variable model that the paper's theory promises, and does it reproduce the VQE expectation values within a target precision? I.e., is the theoretical link 'non-contextual => classically simulable' operationalizable, not just formal?
basis: The paper's punchline is that non-contextual VQE is not a genuine quantum advantage because it admits an efficient classical (noncontextual hidden-variable) simulation. We verified the classifier but never constructed such a model. Kirby-Love (2020) 'Classical simulation of noncontextual Pauli Hamiltonians' provides the construction; independent implementation and benchmarking against the actual VQE trajectory would close the loop.
next_steps: Implement the Kirby-Love 2020 classical simulator for the 2q H2, 4q H2 JW, and 4q H2 BK cases. Compare energy trajectories to VQE at 5-10 bond lengths. Report chemical-accuracy agreement (or lack thereof) and wall-time scaling with |S|. Cross-check against 8-qubit H2O (contextual): the classical simulator should fail or scale badly, providing a negative control.

q: How does the contextuality verdict correlate with alternative quantum-advantage witnesses --- magic (stabilizer rank / mana), von Neumann entanglement entropy of the VQE ground state, and Wigner-function negativity --- on the same six Table I Hamiltonians? Which witness is strictest, and do any witnesses disagree with contextuality (e.g., a non-contextual Hamiltonian whose ground state has high magic, or vice versa)?
basis: The paper implicitly positions contextuality as THE non-classicality witness for VQE. Magic monotones (via stabilizer rank of the ground state), entanglement entropy across a bipartition, and Wigner negativity give correlated but not identical verdicts in the broader QC literature. Disagreements would be scientifically informative: contextuality is defined at the operator/measurement level, magic at the state level; a mismatch signals the two capture different resource axes.
next_steps: For each of the six Table I ground states: (a) compute exact ground state via diagonalization (already have for H2 2q; extend); (b) compute Renyi-2 entropy on a symmetric bipartition; (c) compute stabilizer-rank lower bound via Bravyi-Gosset simulator on <= 8 qubits; (d) if possible, compute discrete Wigner negativity for even-dim subsystems. Build a 6-row table cross-tabulating contextuality (ours), entropy, stabilizer rank, negativity.

q: Does the contextuality classifier's verdict survive hardware noise, or more precisely: at what noise threshold does a nominally-contextual VQE run become indistinguishable from a noncontextual (classically simulable) one when the Hamiltonian expectation values are measured with realistic depolarizing / dephasing noise?
basis: Kirby-Love's classifier is applied to the ideal Pauli Hamiltonian. Physical VQE runs on NISQ hardware sample noisy expectation values. If noise sufficiently damps the specific commutation relations that generate the witness triple, the effective operator set could shift to non-contextual (or become undecidable within finite-shot error bars). This has practical consequences: a hardware VQE claim of 'quantum advantage from contextuality' needs a noise-robustness margin, not just a clean-Hamiltonian verdict.
next_steps: Simulate noisy shot-based estimation (Qiskit Aer noise model with realistic 1q gate error 1e-3, 2q gate error 1e-2, readout error 1e-2) on HeH+ 4q (contextual, CD0=0.38, near boundary). For each shot budget in {1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6}, ask: does the empirically-inferred commutation graph still produce a valid witness triple, or does noise smear it? Plot the shot budget vs. probability of correct verdict. Repeat for LiH and H2O (deeper in the contextual regime) as controls.

q: Does the Theorem 3 classifier extend meaningfully to QAOA cost Hamiltonians and to adiabatic-quantum-computing final Hamiltonians (both are typically Pauli sums like VQE), or does it produce trivially non-contextual verdicts for canonical QAOA problems (Max-Cut, MaxSAT) because those Hamiltonians are diagonal in Z and therefore mutually commuting? If so, is there an appropriate lift of the contextuality-witness idea (perhaps using the driver Hamiltonian and/or the QAOA measurement basis rotation) that recovers a nontrivial classifier for QAOA/AQC advantage claims?
basis: VQE, QAOA, and AQC share the variational Pauli-Hamiltonian structure but differ in ansatz / dynamics. For diagonal Z-only cost Hamiltonians (all Max-Cut QAOA), the operator set is entirely mutually commuting, so T = empty and every such instance is trivially non-contextual --- contradicting the intuition that certain QAOA instances have genuine quantum-speedup potential. Either the classifier is genuinely telling us Max-Cut QAOA has no quantum advantage from contextuality, or the framework needs an extension.
next_steps: (1) Confirm the trivial-non-contextual verdict on Max-Cut QAOA cost Hamiltonians for 3-6 test graphs. (2) Extend the operator set to include the mixer Hamiltonian's Pauli terms (X_i for standard QAOA) and re-run the classifier: does the combined set become contextual? (3) For AQC, apply to the annealed Hamiltonian H(s) = (1-s)H_driver + s H_cost at s=0.5 and compare to s=0, s=1. (4) Write up any positive finding as a short note; even a negative result ('contextuality classifier is trivially degenerate for QAOA cost Hamiltonians alone') is a citable clarification for the QAOA-advantage literature.
